claim: DefaultResourceLoader.reload() discarded the caller's explicit project-trust decision and unconditionally re-applied an untrusted state, so a trusted decision was silently ignored after the bootstrap pass.
changes: packages/coding-agent/src/core/resource-loader.ts: reload() now calls settingsManager.setProjectTrusted(projectTrusted) with the value returned by options.resolveProjectTrust instead of hardcoding false, so the following settingsManager.reload() and packageManager.resolve() use the decided trust state.
.prale-eval/regression.mjs: standalone Node assertion script driving the real reload() lifecycle through .prale-eval/subject.mjs.

validation.notes: Ran from the workspace root with Node 24 (VM modules + TypeScript stripping); exits 0 on the repaired source. The script exercises the production DefaultResourceLoader.reload()/loadProjectTrustExtensions() code with the subject.mjs boundary fakes for initialTrusted in {true,false} and asserts: (1) the bootstrap pass consults resolveProjectTrust with only cli.ts+user.ts and resolves packages with loadedTrust=false, so project extensions stay excluded during bootstrap; (2) for an explicit decision of true, the settings manager receives set(true), settings are reloaded for the trusted state before the final package resolution, the final resolve event carries loadedTrust=true, and loader.getExtensions() contains cli.ts+user.ts+project.ts; (3) for an explicit decision of false with an initially trusted settings manager, no intervening set(false->true) override occurs, the final resolve carries loadedTrust=false, and project.ts is absent; (4) the settings manager ends in the decided trust state. Negative control: temporarily reverting only that line to setProjectTrusted(false) makes the script fail with AssertionError 'final resource resolution ignored the explicit trust decision true: ["resolve",false]' and exit code 1, so the regression detects this stage's original fault. Array values are re-created with Array.from because the subject executes the module in a vm realm (cross-realm prototypes otherwise break assert.deepStrictEqual). Limitation: the checkout has no node_modules and dependencies must not be installed, so the repository's tsc/vitest suites could not be run; validation is limited to this dependency-free Node harness.
